chapters.title: The Risen Lord Gives the Spirit
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 1

It came to pass, after our Lord rose from the dead and appeared to us, and was touched by Thomas and Matthew and John, and we were convinced that our Master had truly risen from the dead, that we fell on our faces and blessed the Father of the new world, God, who has saved us through Jesus Christ our Lord. Held in very great fear, we waited face down, like infants who cannot speak. But Jesus our Lord put His hand on each one of us in turn and lifted us up, saying, "Why has your heart fallen like this? Why are you struck with such astonishment? Do you not know that He who sent Me can do glorious things for the salvation of those who have believed in Him from the heart? Do not stand there astonished and staring, and do not be slack. As children of light, ask My Father who is in heaven for the Spirit of counsel and might, and He will fill you with the Holy Spirit and grant you to be with Me forever."

The Spirit Given

1We answered Him, saying, "Lord, what is the Holy Spirit, and what is His power, that You told us to ask for?" Our Lord said to us, "Truly I tell you, you will not be children of the light except by the Holy Spirit." We answered Him and said, "Our Lord, give us this Spirit." At once Jesus breathed on us. After we had received the Holy Spirit, He said to us, "Truly I tell you: you who have been made disciples for the kingdom of heaven, who have believed in Me with an undoubting heart and have held fast to Me, will be with Me. All who through you know and do the will of My Father, who keep My words and know My sufferings, will be made holy. They will live in the dwellings of My Father and will be delivered from the evil days that are about to come. I will be with them, showing them My ways, in which they will live."

Notes

  • The whole book — worked from the English of J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord (1902), which is translated from the Syriac. No Ge'ez or other source language was used. The Syriac is a sister version of this book: the Ethiopic first Book of the Covenant descends from the same text but differs from it in wording and in places in order. The chapters are Cooper and Maclean's, with their second book numbered on from the first; each verse is one of their paragraphs. The opening narrative, which stands before their chapter 1, is set above verse 1.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Tell Us the Signs of the End
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 2

1Peter and John answered Him and said, "Tell us, our Lord, the signs of the end, and all that will then be done by those who live in this world, so that we too may make them known to those who believe in

2Your name in all the nations, and those generations may watch for them and live." Jesus answered and said, "Did I not tell you some things about the end before I suffered for those who live on the earth?" We answered and said, "Yes, our Lord; but now we want to know the deeds that are the signs of the end of this world, if our Lord has judged it fitting for us to know them, for us and for those who will hear."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Tell us… the signs of the end" — the question the disciples asked on the Mount of Olives, Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age? (Matthew 24:3), asked again after the resurrection.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Son of Destruction
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 3

1Jesus answered and said, "While I was in the world, before I was glorified, I spoke to you of the signs that the end is near: that there will be famines and pestilences on the earth, tumults and commotions, nations rising against nations, and the other things I have told you of. But I commanded you to watch and pray. Now listen, children of the light. My Father, who sent Me to His inheritance, has determined beforehand in His foreknowledge that in the last days, out of the last generation, there will be vessels of grace, holy and honored and chosen. That is why I make known to you exactly what is about to be, and when he will arise, that son of destruction, the Enemy, the Adversary, and what he is like.

Notes

  • v1 "that son of destruction, the Enemy, the Adversary" — Paul's name for him: the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction (2 Thessalonians 2:3). Cooper and Maclean have Son of Perdition.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 4

1There will, then, be signs such as these when the kingdom is approaching. After the famines and pestilences and tumults among the nations, princes will rule and rise to power who love money, who hate the truth, who kill their brothers: liars, haters of the faithful, proud, lovers of gold, joined by kinship but not joined in counsel, for each wants to destroy the life of his fellow. In their armies there will be great affliction, and flight, and bloodshed.

chapters.title: Signs in Heaven and on Earth
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 6

1Then there will be signs in heaven. A bow will be seen, and a horn, and lights; and noises out of season, sounds and ragings of the sea, and a roaring of the earth.

2On the earth there will be signs: dragons born of human beings, and wild beasts likewise; young brides will give birth to babies who speak perfectly and announce the last times, and ask to be put to death. They will look like men far advanced in years; they will be gray-haired when they are born. Women will also bear babies with four feet; some will bear spirits only, and some will bear their offspring with unclean spirits. There will be others who practice divination in the womb and speak with familiar spirits; and there will be many other horrible signs.

chapters.title: Evil Shepherds
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 8

1In the assemblies and the nations and the churches there will be many tumults, for evil shepherds will arise: unjust, lazy, greedy, lovers of pleasure, lovers of gain, lovers of money, talkative, boastful, arrogant, gluttonous, perverse, rash, given to indulgence, vain, opposing the ways of the Gospel and fleeing from the narrow gate, putting every humiliation far from themselves and not grieving for My humiliation, rejecting all the words of truth, despising all the ways of godliness, and not mourning for their sins. So unbelief will spread among the nations, and hatred of the brothers, wickedness, bitterness, laziness, envy, hatred, strife, theft, oppression, drunkenness, debauchery, lewdness, licentiousness, sexual immorality, and all such works as are contrary to the commandments of life. From many, mourning and gentleness will flee away, and peace and meekness, and poverty and godliness, and tears, because the shepherds heard these things and did not do them, and did not even show My commandments, since they themselves are examples of wickedness among the people. The time will come when some of them will deny Me, stir up confusion on the earth, and put their trust in a corruptible king. But those who endure in My name to the end will be saved. Then they will lay down commandments for men, commandments unlike the book of commandments in which the Father is well pleased; and My chosen ones and My holy ones will be rejected by them, and counted among them as the defiled. Yet these are the upright: pure, sorrowful, merciful, quiet, kind, knowing at all times Him who is among them; and they will be called mad for My sake, who have saved them. In those days My Father will gather out of that generation the pure, the pure and faithful souls, to whom I will appear and with whom I will make My dwelling. I will send them the understanding of knowledge and of truth, and the understanding of holiness, and they will not cease to praise and give thanks to their God, My Father who sent Me. They will speak the truth at all times, and they will teach others whose spirit they have tested and found upright and worthy, as for the kingdom, and will instruct them in knowledge and strength and prudence. Those who suffer persecution because they live in godliness will receive the reward of their praise. In those times all the kingdoms will be shaken, and all the world will see affliction and want; this whole world will be counted as nothing, and all its possessions will be destroyed by many destroyers. There will be a great scarcity of crops, and the winter will be very severe. The princes who rule over gold and silver and are rich in all that is in this world will be few and small; and the children of this world will hold the storerooms and barns, and will rule over the markets of buying and selling. Many will be afflicted, and so will call on their God to be delivered. Blessed are those who are not alive at that time; and blessed also are those who are alive and endure. For when these things come to pass, she who is in labor is near to giving birth, for the time is fulfilled.

Notes

  • v1 "fleeing from the narrow gate… those who endure in My name to the end will be saved" — the Lord's words in the Gospel: How narrow is the gate and hard the road that leads to life (Matthew 7:14), and the one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 24:13).

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Nations Struck
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 10

1Syria will be plundered and will weep for her sons. Cilicia will lift up her neck until He who judges her appears. The daughter of Babylon will rise from the throne of her glory, to drink the wine that is mixed for her. Cappadocia, Lycia and Lycaonia will bow their backs, for many multitudes will be corrupted by the decay of their wickedness. Then the camps of the barbarians will be opened, and many chariots will go out, so as to cover the face of the earth. In all Armenia, and in Pontus and in Bithynia, the young men will fall by the sword, and the sons and the daughters will be taken captive. The sons and daughters of Lycaonia will be mingled in their blood. Pisidia, which boasts and trusts in her riches, will be thrown down to the ground. The sword will pass through Phoenicia, because her people are children of corruption. Judea will clothe herself in mourning, and will be made ready for the day of destruction, because of her uncleanness. Then she will gather together the abomination of desolation. The East will be opened by him, and the roads will be opened by him. Sword and flame are in his hands; he burns with anger and fiery rage. This is the armor of the judgment of the corruption of those born on the earth: the destruction of the faithful, the way of bloodshed. For his way is in error, his power is to blaspheme, his hand is for deceit, his right hand in misery, and his left hand in darkness.

Notes

  • v1 "the daughter of Babylon… to drink the wine that is mixed for her" — Revelation's word on Babylon, in the cup she mixed, mix her a double portion (Revelation 18:6).

  • v1 "the abomination of desolation" — the words of the Gospel, when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (Matthew 24:15).

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Set the Church in Order
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 14

1"I have told you these things, then, so that wherever you go you may test the souls that are holy, and tell them what is fitting and right, and what is about to be, and all that I gave you as commandments before I was glorified, so that believing them they may truly live. From now on will be the beginning of birth pains, and the mystery of destruction. Turn, then, to the Church: set it right, put it in due order and arrange it, doing all things in uprightness and holiness. Speak to each one in the way that helps him, so that your Father who is in heaven may be glorified. Be wise, so that you may persuade those held captive by error and those sunk in ignorance, so that, coming to the knowledge of God and living devoutly and purely, they may praise My Father and your God."

Notes

  • v1 "the beginning of birth pains… My Father and your God" — the Lord's words on the signs of the end, All these are the beginning of birth pains (Matthew 24:8), and the risen Lord's words to Mary, I am going up to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God (John 20:17). Here the signs end and the order of the Church begins.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Teach Us About the Head of the Church
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 15

1After Jesus had spoken these words, Peter and John and Thomas and Matthew and Andrew and Matthias and the rest said, "Our Lord, truly You have spoken words of warning and of truth to us now as well. Though we are not worthy, You have given us many things, and You have granted to those of future generations who are worthy to know Your words and to flee from the snares of the Evil One. But, our Lord, we ask You: make Your perfect light shine on us, and on those who are foreordained and set apart to be Yours. Because we have asked You many times, we pray You, teach us what kind of man the one who stands at the head of the Church ought to be, and by what rule he should raise up and order the Church. For it is urgent, when we are sent to the nations to preach the salvation that comes from You, that we do not miss how the mysteries of the Church ought to be arranged. So we want to learn from Your mouth, our Savior and Perfecter, leaving nothing out, how the chief of the holy things ought to please You, and likewise all who minister in Your Church."

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

1Jesus also said to us, "Since you too have asked Me about the rule of the Church, I hand on and make known to you how you ought to order and instruct the one who stands at the head of the Church, and to keep the perfect, just and most excellent rule, in which My Father who sent Me is well pleased. chapters.title: The House of the Church
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 18

My Mysteries for My Own

1"But because among the gathered people there are more and more fleshly desires, and the workers are weak and few, only My perfect workers will know My words in their fullness, all that I spoke to you at times in private before I suffered, which you know: you have them and understand them. For My mysteries are given to those who are Mine, with whom I will rejoice and be glad with My Father. When they are set free from this life, they will come to Me.

2But speak the rest of these words in the churches, setting them out and appointing them.

3From the day My faithful ones also desire to know whatever is in this testament of Mine, so that they may do the things of My Father, I will be with them and be praised among them, and I will make My dwelling with them, teaching them by power the will of My Father.

4See that you do not give My holy things to the dogs, or throw pearls before pigs, as I have often commanded you.

5Do not give My holy things to defiled and wicked people who do not carry My cross and are not subject to Me; My commandments would be mocked among them. For the one who is embittered, who does not do them but gives My words away to no profit, it will be the destruction of their souls.

6But it will be spoken and given to those who are firm and settled and do not fall away, who keep My commandments and this tradition, so that, keeping them, they may remain holy and upright and strong in Me, fleeing from the downfall of wickedness and the death of sin. The Holy Spirit also gives them His grace, so that they may believe rightly, may know spiritually, in the Spirit, the things of the Spirit, may endure labor in hope, serve My Gospel in joy, and bear the reproach of My cross, not doubting but rather glorying. For truly I tell you, such men and such women as these will live, after death, in the third order of My Father who sent Me.

The Church Building

7I tell you, then, how the sanctuary ought to be; then I will make known the holy rule of the priests of the Church.

8Let the church, then, be like this: let it have three entrances, as a type of the Trinity.

9Let the deacons' room be to the right of the right-hand entrance, so that the eucharists, the offerings that are brought, may be seen. Let there be a forecourt, with a portico running around it, up to the deacons' room.

11Then inside the forecourt let there be a place for a baptistery, twenty-one cubits long, as a type of all the prophets, and twelve cubits wide, as a type of those appointed to preach the Gospel, with one entrance and three exits.

12Let the church have a house for the catechumens, which will also be the house of the exorcists. Let it not stand apart from the church, but be placed so that those who enter it and are in it may hear the readings, the spiritual hymns of praise and the psalms.

13Let there be a throne by the altar, with the places of the presbyters on the right and on the left: on the right let those sit who are more exalted and honored, and those who labor in the word, and on the left those of middle age. Let the place where the throne is be raised three steps, for the altar ought to be there.

14Let that house have two porches, on the right and on the left, for men and for women.

15Let all the places be lit, both as a type and for reading.

16Let the altar have a veil of pure linen, for it is without spot.

17Let the baptistery likewise be under a veil.

18Let a place be built for remembrance, so that the priest and the chief deacon, sitting with the readers, may write the names of those who bring the offerings, or of those for whom they have brought them, so that when the holy things are offered by the bishop, the reader or the chief deacon may name them in remembrance, which the priests and the people offer for them with prayer. For this type is in heaven too.

19Let the place of the presbyters be inside the veil, beside the place of remembrance.

20Let the house of the offering and the treasury be right beside the deacons' room.

21But let the place of reading be a little outside the altar.

22Let the bishop's house be beside the place called the forecourt,

23and that of the widows who are called 'those who sit in front.'

24Let that of the presbyters and deacons be behind the baptistery.

25Let the deaconesses stay beside the door of the Lord's house.

26Let the church have a guest house nearby, where the chief deacon will receive strangers.

Notes

  • v6 "know spiritually, in the Spirit, the things of the Spirit" — Paul's words: The natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God… because they are judged spiritually (1 Corinthians 2:14).

  • v7 — the heading of Cooper and Maclean's chapter 19 cannot be read in the scan held here, so its text stands with chapter 18. Where chapter 19 begins is not certain; the turn from the testament's words (vv1–6) to the building of the church (v7) is the likeliest place.

  • v10 — the paragraph numbered 10 in the text held here is the edition's footnotes to vv5–6, not part of the text, so no verse stands there.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Bishop Chosen
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 20

1"When the house has been built as is fitting and right, let the bishop be appointed, chosen by all the people according to the will of the Holy Spirit. Let him be without fault, chaste, quiet, gentle, free of anxiety, watchful, not a lover of money, blameless, not quarrelsome, ready to forgive, a teacher, not a man of many words, a lover of what is good, a lover of labor, a lover of widows, a lover of orphans, a lover of the poor, experienced in the mysteries, not slack and distracted by the company of this world, peaceful, and complete in every good thing, as one to whom the order and the place of God are entrusted. It is good that he be without a wife, but at least that he has been the husband of one wife only, so that he may sympathize with the weakness of widows. Let him be appointed when he is of middle age, not a youth.

Notes

  • v1 "not a lover of money… the husband of one wife only" — Paul's list for the overseer: the husband of one wife… not quarrelsome, not a lover of money (1 Timothy 3:2–3). Here the rule has a reason Paul does not give: so that he may sympathize with the weakness of widows.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Ordination of a Bishop
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 21

1"When he is such a man, let him be ordained on the first day of the week, with all agreeing to his appointment and bearing witness to him, together with all the neighboring presbyters and bishops. Let those bishops lay hands on him, having first washed their hands, while the presbyters stand beside them without speaking, in fear, lifting up their hearts in silence.

2After that, let the bishops lay hands on him, saying:

3'We lay hands on the servant of God, who has been chosen in the Spirit, for the true and devout ordering of the Church of the invisible and living God, which alone has the rule and is not dissolved; and for the giving of true judgment and of divine and holy revelations, of divine gifts and of faithful teachings of the Trinity, by the cross, by the resurrection, by the incorruption, in the holy Church of God.'

4After this, let one bishop, at the bidding of the other bishops, lay hands on him, saying the words of his appointment, like this:

5The Prayer of Ordination of a Bishop

6'O God, who made all things in power and established them, and founded the inhabited world in reason, and adorned the crown of all that You made; who gave them to keep Your commandments in fear; who gave us the understanding of the truth, and made known to us that good Spirit of Yours; who sent Your beloved Son, the only Savior, without spot, for our salvation: O God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Father of compassion and God of all comfort, who live forever in the pure heights; who are high and worthy of worship, fearful and great; who see all things and know all things before they are, with whom all things were before they were made; who gave light to the Church by the grace of Your Only-begotten Son, having foreordained from the beginning those who delight in what is just and do what is holy, to live in Your dwellings; who chose Abraham, who pleased You by his faith, and took holy Enoch up to the treasure house of life; who have set princes and priests in order in Your sanctuary above: O Lord, who called them to praise and glorify Your name and the name of Your Only-begotten in the place of Your glory; O Lord God, who before the foundation of the world did not leave Your sanctuary above without a ministry, and since the foundation of the world have adorned and glorified Your sanctuaries on earth with faithful princes and priests, after the pattern of Your own heaven: You, Lord, are well pleased even now to be praised, and have granted that there be princes for Your people. Make shine and pour out understanding, and the grace that comes from Your princely Spirit, which You gave to Your beloved Son Jesus Christ. Give wisdom, O God, give reasoning, strength, power, unity of spirit, to do all things with Your help. Give the Spirit that is Yours, O holy God; send to Your holy and pure Church, and to every place that sings "Holy" to You, Him who was given to Your Holy One. Grant, O Lord, that this servant of Yours may please You in giving You glory and praise without ceasing, O God, in fitting hymns of praise and at suitable times, in acceptable prayers, in faithful asking, with an upright mind and a meek heart, in the working of life and of meekness and of truth, in the knowledge of uprightness. O Father, who know the hearts, grant to this servant of Yours, whom You have chosen to be bishop, to feed Your holy flock, and to stand at the head of the priesthood without fault, serving You day and night. Grant that Your face may be seen by him. Grant, O Lord, that he may offer You the offerings of Your holy Church carefully and with all fear. Give him to have Your powerful Spirit, to loose every bond, as You gave Him to Your apostles, so that he may please You in meekness. Fill him with love, knowledge, understanding, discipline, completeness, strength and a pure heart, when he prays for the people, and when he mourns for those who act foolishly and draws them to receive help, and when he offers You praises and thanksgivings and prayers as a soothing aroma, through Your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom praise and honor and might are given to You, with the Holy Spirit, before the ages, and now, and at all times, and forever and ever without end. Amen.'

7Let the people say, 'Amen,' and then let them cry out, 'He is worthy, he is worthy, he is worthy.'

8After he is ordained, let the people keep the feast three days, for the mystery that on the third day our

9Lord rose from the dead. Let everyone give him the Peace.

Notes

  • v6 "Father of compassion and God of all comfort… took holy Enoch up" — Paul's blessing, the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and God of all comfort (2 Corinthians 1:3); and Enoch, who was taken up so that he did not see death (Hebrews 11:5).

  • vv8–9 "three days… our / Lord rose" — one sentence across two of the edition's paragraphs, kept as it divides them.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Bishop's Rule of Life
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 22

1"Let him be constant at the altar. Let him persist in prayer day and night, above all at the fixed hours of the night: at the first hour, at midnight, and at early twilight, when the morning star rises; then also in the morning, and at the third, sixth and ninth hours, and at the twelfth hour, at the lighting of the lamps. If he also offers prayers without ceasing at every hour, for the people and for himself, he does well. Let him stay in the house of the Church alone. If he has one or two of like mind with him, it is good for him to be with them, to pray together as one. For you know that I have told you: where two or three are gathered in My name, I am among them. If he cannot stay all night, let him at least keep the hours I have named, for then the angels visit the Church.

2Let him fast three days each week all the year. But for three weeks after his appointment let him keep the fast by the number of the eighteen Exalted Entrances through which the Only-begotten passed when He came to His passion. On the first day of the week only, let him eat bread with oil and honey and salt, and all the fruits of trees; but let him not taste wine at all, except the cup of the Offering alone, whether he is sick or well, for it is good that this be for the priests only. After these weeks, all the year, let him fast three days each week, and for the rest of the time fast as his strength allows. Let him not eat meat at all: not that he is to blame if he tastes or eats it, but because, when he has chosen weakness, such strong food does not fit, and so that he may keep watch.

3Let the Offering be only on the Sabbath, on the first day of the week, and on a fast day. On the eve let him instruct and teach these things as a mystery to those he has tested as having ears to hear. If he is sick in body, let him quickly see to his healing, eating fish and taking a little of the wine of the holy things regularly, so that the Church does not also come to an end because he lies sick, but those who learn may have joy. When he teaches in the Church, let him speak carefully, as a man who knows that he speaks for a testimony the teaching of the whole ministry of the Father of all, the teaching that is accurately written. Let him say all these things, all that he knows accurately and has long remembered. For if he knows what he is saying, he may hope that his hearers will have known these things too. With all his labor let him plead with the Lord that his word may bear the fruits of the Holy Spirit in those who hear.

4Let him do everything in order and with knowledge. Let him dismiss the catechumens after he has admonished them with the meditations and admonitions of the Prophets and Apostles and with instructive words, so that they may know Him whom they confess. But let him teach the faithful as a mystery, having first dismissed the catechumens; and after the teaching of the mysteries let him offer, so that, knowing in what mystery they share, they may offer with fear.

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Offering
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 23

The Loaves and the Order

1"Let him offer three loaves on the Sabbath, as a complete symbol of the Trinity, but on the first day of the week four loaves, as a complete symbol of the Gospel.

2Because the people of old went astray, when he offers let the veil in front of the door be closed, and within it let him offer with the presbyters and deacons and the enrolled widows, the subdeacons and deaconesses and readers, and those who have gifts. Let the bishop stand first, in the middle, and the presbyters right behind him on either side; the widows right behind the presbyters on the left side, and the deacons behind the presbyters on the right side; the readers behind them, the subdeacons behind the readers, and the deaconesses behind the subdeacons.

3Then let the bishop place his hand on the loaves that have been set on the altar, and let the presbyters place their hands with his, and let the rest only stand.

4Let the loaf of a catechumen not be received, not even if he has a believing son or wife and wishes to offer on their behalf; let it not be offered unless he is baptized.

5Before the bishop or presbyter offers, let the people give the Peace to one another.

6Then, when a great silence has fallen, let the deacon say this:

The Deacon's Admonition

7The Deacon's Admonition at the Eucharist. 'Lift up your hearts to heaven.

8If anyone is angry with his companion, let him be reconciled.

9If anyone has a conscience without faith, let him confess it.

10If anyone has a thought foreign to the commandments, let him depart.

11If anyone has fallen into sin, let him not hide: he cannot hide.

12If anyone's reason is disordered, let him not draw near.

13If anyone is defiled, if anyone is not firm, let him give place.

14If anyone is a stranger to the commandments of Jesus, let him depart.

15If anyone despises the prophets, let him separate himself; let him deliver himself from the wrath of the Only-begotten.

16Let us not despise the cross.

17Let us flee from the threat.

18We have our Lord watching us: the Father of lights, with the Son, and the angels who visit us.

19See to yourselves, that you are not angry with your neighbors.

20See that no one is in anger: God sees. Lift up your hearts to offer for the salvation of life and of holiness.

21In the wisdom of God let us receive the grace that has been given us.'

22Then let the bishop, giving thanks, say with an awed voice, 'Our Lord be with you.' Let the people say, 'And with your spirit.'

23Let the bishop say, 'Lift up your hearts.' Let the people say, 'They are lifted up to the Lord.' Let the bishop say, 'Let us give thanks to the Lord.'

24Let all the people say, 'It is fitting and right.'

25Let the bishop cry out, 'Holy things in the holy.'

26Let the people call out, 'In heaven and on earth without ceasing.'

The Thanksgiving

27The Eucharist, or Thanksgiving, over the Offering.

28Let the bishop at once say: 'We give You thanks, O God, the Holy One, Strengthener of our souls and Giver of our life, the Treasure of incorruption, and Father of the Only-begotten, our Savior, whom in the last times You sent to us as Savior and Herald of Your purpose. For it is Your purpose that we should be saved in You. Our heart gives You thanks, O Lord, our mind, our soul, with all its thinking, that Your grace may come upon us, O Lord, so that we may always praise You, and Your Only-begotten Son, and Your Holy Spirit, now and always, and forever and ever. Amen.

29O Power of the Father, Grace of the nations, Knowledge, true Wisdom, Exaltation of the meek, Medicine of souls, Confidence of us who believe — for You are the Strength of the righteous, the Hope of the persecuted, the Haven of those tossed by the storm, the Light of the perfect, the Son of the living God — make rise on us, out of Your gift that cannot be searched out, courage, might, trust, wisdom, strength, unfailing faith, unshaken hope, the knowledge of Your Spirit, meekness and uprightness, so that always, O Lord, we Your servants and all the people may praise You purely, bless You, give thanks to You, Lord, at all times, and pray to You.'

30Let the bishop also say:

31'You, Lord, Founder of the heights and King of the treasuries of light, Visitor of the heavenly Zion, King of the orders of archangels, of Dominions, Praises, Thrones, Raiments, Lights, Joys, Delights; Father of kings, who hold all in Your hand and provide for all by Your reason, through Your Only-begotten Son, who was crucified for our sins: You, Lord, sent Your Word, who is of Your counsel and covenants, through whom You made all things, being well pleased with Him, into a virgin womb. When He was conceived and made flesh, He was shown to be Your Son, born of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin. Fulfilling Your will and preparing a holy people, He stretched out His hands to suffering, to set free from sufferings and corruption and death those who have hoped in You. When He was betrayed to the suffering He chose, that He might raise up those who had slipped, find those who were lost, give life to the dead, loose the pains of death, tear apart the bonds of the Devil, fulfill the counsel of the Father, tread down Sheol, open the way of life, guide the righteous to light, fix the boundary, light up the darkness, nurture the infants and reveal the resurrection, He took bread and gave it to His disciples, saying, "Take, eat, this is My body, which is broken for you for the forgiveness of sins. When you do this, you make My resurrection." The cup of wine that He mixed He also gave, as a type of the blood that He shed for us.

32Remembering, then, Your death and resurrection, we offer You bread and the cup, giving thanks to You, who alone are God forever, and our Savior, since You have promised us that we may stand before You and serve You as priests. So we give You thanks, we Your servants, O Lord.'

33Let the people say the same.

34Let the bishop also say: 'We offer You this thanksgiving, Eternal Trinity, O

35Lord Jesus Christ, O Lord the Father, before whom all creation and every nature trembles, fleeing into itself, O Lord the Holy Spirit. We have brought You this drink and this food of Your holiness. Make it be for us not for condemnation, not for reproach, not for destruction, but for the healing and support of our spirit. Yes, O God, grant that by Your name every thought of what displeases You may flee away. Grant, O God, that every proud thought may be driven from us by Your name, which is written within the veils of Your sanctuaries on high: the name at which Sheol is amazed when it hears it, the deep is torn open, the spirits are driven away, the dragon is crushed, unbelief is cast out, disobedience is subdued, anger is calmed, envy does not work, pride is rebuked, greed is rooted out, boasting is taken away, arrogance is humbled, and every root of bitterness is destroyed. Sustain to the end those who have gifts of revelation. Strengthen those who have a gift of healing. Make those courageous who have the power of tongues. Keep upright those who have the word of teaching. Care always for those who do Your will. Visit the widows. Help the orphans. Remember those who have fallen asleep in the faith. 36Your saints, and give us the power to please You as they too pleased You. Feed the people in uprightness. 37The deacon: 'Let us earnestly pray our Lord and our God to give us harmony of spirit.'

38The bishop: 'Give us harmony in the Holy Spirit, and heal our souls by this offering, so that we may live in You through all the ages of ages.'

39Let the people also pray in the same words.

40After these things, the seal of the thanksgiving, like this: 'Blessed be the name of the Lord forever.'

41The priest: 'Blessed is He who has come in the name of the Lord. Blessed is the name of His praise.'

42Let all the people say, 'So be it, so be it.'

43Let the bishop say, 'Send the grace of the Spirit upon us.'

Receiving

44If the bishop is unclean, let him not offer, but let a presbyter offer. Let him not receive of the mystery either, not as though he were defiled, but for the honor of the altar. After he has fasted and bathed in pure water, let him come near and serve. A presbyter likewise. If a widow is in her monthly period, let her not come near. Likewise, if a woman or a layman or any of the clergy is unclean, let them not come near, for the honor of the altar, except after fasting and bathing.

45Let the priests receive first, in this order: the bishops, presbyters, deacons, widows, readers, subdeacons; after these, those who have gifts, the newly baptized, the infants. The people in this order: old men, virgins, and the rest. The women: deaconesses, and after them the rest.

46When each one receives the thanksgiving, let him say 'Amen' before he partakes. After that let him pray like this; after he receives the Eucharist, let him say, 'Holy, Holy, Holy, Trinity beyond words, grant me to receive this body for life and not for condemnation. Grant me to bear the fruits that please You, so that when I am shown to be pleasing to You I may live in You, doing Your commandments, and may call You Father with boldness when I call for Your kingdom and Your will to come to me. May Your name be hallowed in me, O Lord, for You are mighty and worthy of praise, and to You be praise forever and ever. Amen.'

47After the prayer let him receive.

48When he takes of the cup, let him say 'Amen' twice, as a complete symbol of the body and the blood.

49When all have received, let them pray, giving thanks for what they have received, the deacon saying:

50'Let us give thanks to the Lord, as we receive His holy things, so that receiving them may be for the life and salvation of our souls. Let us ask and plead for His grace, lifting up praise to the Lord our God.'

51After that let the bishop say:

52'O Lord, Giver of eternal light, Helmsman of souls, Guide of the saints, give us eyes of understanding that always look to You, and ears that hear You only, so that our soul may be filled with grace. Create in us a clean heart, O God, so that we may always grasp Your greatness. O God, Wonderful, who love mankind, make our souls better, and by this Eucharist that we Your servants, who fall short in much, have received, shape our thoughts so that they do not swerve. For Your kingdom is blessed, O Lord God, glorified and praised in Father and in Son and in Holy Spirit, before the ages, and now, and always, and for the ages and forever and ever without end.'

Notes

  • v31 "When you do this, you make My resurrection" — so the Syriac as Cooper and Maclean give it. In Paul the words over the bread end Do this in remembrance of Me (1 Corinthians 11:24); here what the Church does is tied to the resurrection, as in the prayer that follows, Remembering, then, Your death and resurrection (v32).

  • v46 "call You Father… Your kingdom and Your will… May Your name be hallowed in me" — the Lord's Prayer, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come, Your will be done (Matthew 6:9–10), prayed by each one who receives, with in me and to me.

  • vv34–35, 35–36 — two sentences that run across the edition's paragraphs, kept as it divides them.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Oil for Healing
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 24

1"If the priest consecrates oil for the healing of those who suffer, let him say this, quietly placing the vessel before the altar:

2'O Lord God, who have given us the Spirit, the Advocate, the Lord, the saving and unshaken Name, hidden from the foolish but revealed to the wise; O Christ, who sanctified us, and by Your mercies make the servants You choose wise with the wisdom that is Yours; who sent the knowledge of Your Spirit to us sinners by the holiness that is Yours, giving us the power of the Spirit; who are the Healer of every sickness and every suffering; who gave the gift of healing to those You counted worthy of it: send on this oil, the type of Your richness, the delivering power of Your good compassion, so that it may deliver those who labor, heal those who are sick, and sanctify those who return, when they come to Your faith; for You are mighty and worthy of praise forever and ever.'

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Morning Praise
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 26

The First Hymn of the Dawn

1"At early dawn let the bishop gather the people, so that the service may be finished before the sun rises.

2When he says the First Hymn of Praise, of the Dawn, with the presbyters and deacons and the rest, and the faithful too, standing close by, let him say this:

3Let the people say, 'It is fitting and right.'

4The bishop: 'It is fitting and right that we should praise and extol and give thanks to You, who made all things, God beyond words. Stretching our souls upward, we raise to You, O Lord, a hymn of praise for the morning: to You who are all-wise, powerful, great in mercies, O God, Strengthener and Raiser-up of our souls. We praise You, the Word, begotten of the Father before the ages, who rest alone with Your saints, who are praised with the hymns of the archangels; You the Maker, who were not made with hands, who make known holy things that are invisible, pure and spotless; You who have made known to us the hidden mysteries of wisdom, and promised us immortal light. We lift up praise to You in pure holiness, we Your servants, O Lord.'

5Let the people say, 'We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, O Lord; and we pray to You, O our God.'

6The bishop also: 'O God, Begetter of light, Source of life, Giver of knowledge, Gift of grace, Maker of souls, who make what is beautiful, Giver of the Holy Spirit, Treasure of wisdom and Maker of good things, the Lord, Teacher of holiness, who rule the ages by Your will, Receiver of pure prayers: we praise You, the Only-begotten Son, the Firstborn and Word of the Father, who gave all Your grace to us who call on You, the Helper, and on the Father who begot You; whose being cannot be harmed, where neither moth nor worm destroys; who give to all who trust in You with all their heart the things the angels have longed to look into; Guardian of eternal light and of treasures that do not decay; who by the will of Your Father have shed light on the darkness in us; who raised us from the depth to light; who gave us life out of death, and freedom out of slavery; who by the cross made us members of Your Father's household, by Your gospel guided us to the heights of heaven, and comforted us by Your prophets; who in Your own person made us members of the household of God the Father of lights: grant us, O Lord, to praise You, our God, so that we may always speak Your praise with unceasing thanksgiving, we Your servants, O Lord.'

7The people: 'We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, we pray to You, O our God.'

8The bishop also: 'We sing to You with our mouths this threefold hymn of praise, as a figure of Your kingdom, O Son of God, who are from eternity; who are above all, with the Father; whom all creation praises, trembling with fear of Your Spirit; before whom all nature trembles in fear, and whom every soul of the righteous blesses; in whom all of us have taken refuge; who have made confusion, storms and wind cease from us; who have been to us a haven of rest and a refuge from corruption; in whom we hope for eternal salvation; who give calm weather to those tossed on the seas and in the storms; who are called upon in sickness and heal without price; who are with those shut up in prison; who loosed us from the bonds of death; Comforter of the poor, of those who mourn, and of those who have labored and worn themselves out with the cross; who turn away every threat from us; who have rebuked the cunning of Satan for us; who drive away his threats and give us courage; who thrust all error away from those who trust in You; whom the prophets and apostles praised in secret: we praise You, O Lord, we lift up glory to You, so that, having known You, we may rest in the dwellings of life, always doing Your will. Grant us, O Lord, to walk by Your commandments, and in mercy visit us all, small and great, the prince and his people, the shepherd and his flock; for You, O Lord, are our God, and blessed and praised is Your kingdom, the kingdom of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, before the ages, and now, and always, and for the ages, and forever and ever without end.'

9Let the people say, 'Amen.'

10Let them sing psalms and four hymns of praise: one by Moses, and of Solomon, and of the other prophets; like this: little singing boys; two virgins; three deacons; three presbyters. Let the hymn of praise then be said by the bishop or by one of the presbyters.

The Hymn of the Seal

11Let it be said like this: 'The grace of our Lord be with you all.' Let the people say, 'And with your spirit.'

12Let the priest say, 'Let us also praise our Lord.'

13Let the people say, 'It is fitting and right.' Let the priest say, 'Let your hearts be steadfast.' Let the people say, 'We hold them steadfast with the Lord.'

14The Hymn of Praise of the Seal.

15'O Lord, the Father, Giver of light, Author of all power and of all spirits, Sealer of eternal light and Guide of life, Maker of happiness and immortality, who brought us through the darkness of matter and gave us light that is not of matter; who loosed the bonds of disobedience and crowned us with the faith that is Yours; who do not keep far from Your servants, but are in them always; who do not neglect the souls that pray to You with labor and in Your fear; who know all things before they are thought, search out all things before they are considered, and give what You will give before we ask You; who are well pleased to hear those who serve You with an undoubting heart, O King of the highest lights and of the army of heaven, who hear the archangels when they praise You, and are pleased with them: answer us, O Lord, we pray You. Grant us with boldness, with unceasing voice, to praise You, to extol You, to lift up glory to You, so that, guarded by You and guided in light, we Your servants, O Lord, may praise You always.'

16The people: 'We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, O Lord; and we pray to You, O our God.'

17The priest: 'O Lord Jesus, hear us, O Holy One, who were the Voice of the mute and of those without reason, the Strength of the paralyzed, Giver of light to the blind, Guide of the lame, Cleanser of the lepers, Healer of bodily flows, Healer of the deaf and mute, Rebuker of death, Tormentor of darkness, the Ray of light, the Lamp that is not put out, the Sun that is not darkened and does not rest, but always gives light to Your saints; who have fitted all things together in a fair likeness of beauty; who are the well-tempered Reason; who have given light openly to all; Savior of the sons of men and Turner of souls; who provide all things as is right, Maker of the angels, who adorn all; the Thought of the Father; who founded the ages in prudence and wisdom and fitted them together, and were sent to us from Your eternal Father; the Understanding of the Spirit, who cannot be grasped or understood, the Revealer of things invisible: You are glorious, and Your name is Wonderful. So we also, Your servants, O Lord, give You praise.'

18The people: 'We praise You, we bless You, we give thanks to You, O Lord; we pray to You, O our Lord.'

19The priest: 'We sing, O holy Lord, this threefold hymn of praise to You, who gave us a faith in You that cannot be loosed, by which You made us conquer the bonds of death; who created upright minds in those who trust in You, so that they might be gods; who by the Spirit gave us to tread underfoot all the power of the enemy, so that we may not profane what may not be profaned; who by Your mediation have made friendship for us with Your Father. Answer us, Your servants, O Lord, whom we entreat without ceasing, who at our prayer give us power against the adversary, whom we ask always for the overthrow of the Evil One. chapters.title: The Teaching of the Mysteries
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 28

Him We Confess

1"After that let the bishop teach the mysteries to the people. If he is not present, let a presbyter speak, so that the faithful may know whom they are drawing near to, and who is their God and Father. Then let the teaching of the mysteries be said like this. The Initiation into the Mysteries, which is said to the faithful before the Offering. 'We confess Him who was before all, and was present, and is, and is coming; who suffered and was buried, and rose, and was glorified by the Father; who loosed our cords from death, who rose from the dead; who is not only Man but God as well; who by the Holy Spirit restored the flesh of Adam, with his soul, to immortality, because He kept Adam by the Spirit; who clothed Himself with dead Adam and made him live; who went up into heaven; under whom, after the cross, Death fell and was conquered, when its bonds were dissolved, by which the Devil once grew strong and prevailed against us; through whose passion Death was shown to be useless and weak, when Jesus cut its cords and its power, when its snares were cut and He struck it in the face, and Death, filled with darkness, was shaken and afraid as it saw the Only-begotten Son; who in His human soul went down, in the Godhead, into Sheol; who came down from the pure heights above the heavens. Him we confess, the undivided Thought who is from the Father and of one will with Him; Him, the Maker of heaven with His Father, who is the Crown of the angels, the Strength of the archangels, the Raiment of the hosts and the Spirit of the Dominions; Him, the Ruler of the everlasting kingdom and Prince of the saints, the unfathomable Understanding of the Father; Him who is the Wisdom, the Power, the Lord, the Thought, the Understanding, the Hand, the Arm of the Father.

2As we believe, we confess Him who is our Light, Salvation, Savior, Protector, Helper, Teacher, Deliverer, Rewarder, Supporter, Strength, Wall; our Shepherd, Entrance, Door, Way,

3Life, Medicine, Provision, Drink and Judge. We confess Him able to suffer yet not able to suffer, Son yet not created, dead yet alive, the Son of the Father, beyond grasp yet grasped; who, sinless Himself, bore our sins when He left the Father's heaven; whose body, broken, becomes our salvation, and His blood and Spirit our life and holiness, and the water our cleansing; who gives light to the hearts of those who fear Him, being with them in all things; who has made us strangers to the whole way of the Devil; the Renewer of souls, in whom we have all put our trust.

The Word Made Flesh

4He, being God, eternal God before the ages with the Father, when He saw the world perishing in the bonds of sin, trodden down by the power of a cunning wild beast, and made subject to death through ignorance and error, resolved to heal the human race. He came to a virgin womb, hidden from all the camps of the heavenly ones, and cast the opposing hosts into ignorance. When He, the Incorruptible, clothed Himself with corruptible flesh, making flesh that was under death incorruptible, He showed in the flesh of dead Adam, with which He clothed Himself, an example of incorruption, and by that example the things of corruption were done away.

5He gave holy commandments through the Gospel, which proclaims the kingdom beforehand. By this Gospel, as a figure of the kingdom, we learned to live; through this Gospel the bonds of the Devil have been cut, so that we may reach immortality instead of death, and instead of ignorance may receive the grace of watchfulness.

6So He, the Son of God, the Lord, became Man. He took on the dead race of Adam in all its kinds by emptying Himself; He who is the First came to birth as Man, though He is God; He who was foreknown by the prophets, preached by the apostles, praised by angels and glorified by the Father of all was crucified for us. His cross is our life, our strength, our salvation, for it is the hidden mystery, the joy beyond words, and through it the whole nature of mankind, always bearing it, is made one with God and not to be parted from Him. For it is the kindly power, never parted from God, that these lips cannot speak as is fitting, that was hidden from the beginning; but now the mystery that is revealed, which is for the faithful, will be, not as it seems to be, but as it is.

7This is the cross in which we boast, so that we may be glorified; and those who carry it, the faithful and perfect, separate their souls from everything that can be felt and everything that is seen, as from something not true. By it ask for yourselves, you who act like men: make your visible ears deaf, make your bodily eyes blind, so that you may know the will of Christ and the whole mystery of your salvation. Holy men and women, whose part it is to boast in the Lord, listen to the inner man.

Death Cries Out

8Our Lord, when He taught us and appointed a covenant for us and made us members of His household, came after His passion into Sheol and took all the earth captive. He made the nature of death captive to life. When Death saw Him going down in His soul into Sheol, it was deceived, and hoped He was food for it, as was its custom. But when it saw in Him the beauty of the Godhead, it cried out aloud, saying: "Who is this who has clothed Himself with Man, who was under me, and has conquered me? Who is this who snatches from destruction flesh that was bound by me? Who is this who has clothed Himself with earth, but is Himself heaven? Who is this who was born into corruption, but suffers no corruption? Who is this, a stranger to my laws? Who is this who takes captive those who are mine? Who is this who strives with the power of burning Death, and conquers darkness? What is this new glory in this sight, which keeps me from doing what I would? Who is this new dead One without sin? Who is this who by the abundance of light puts out darkness, and does not let me rule over those who are mine, but draws to heaven the souls that were given to me? What is this glory that keeps the body from decay? Who is this whom I cannot touch? What is this glory, past searching out by all around it? Woe is me! I am put to flight by Him and by those who are His, for I cannot harm them."

9He is the Christ who was crucified, by whom what was on the left was placed on the right, what was beneath became as what was above, and what was behind as what was before. When He rose from the dead and trod down Sheol and by death killed Death, after He rose on the third day, He gave thanks to the Father, saying: "I give thanks to You, O My Father, not with these lips that are fixed together, nor with a bodily tongue through which truth and lying go out, nor with this created and material word; but I give thanks to You, the King, with that Voice which through You understands all things, which does not come by a bodily organ, which does not fall on fleshly ears, which —

When It Is Said

10After the people are taught the Initiation into the mysteries, let the Eucharist be offered. But let the Initiation into the mysteries not be said each time, only at Pascha, on the Sabbath, on the first day of the week, and on the days of Epiphany and of Pentecost.

Notes

  • v1 "was before all, and was present, and is, and is coming" — the title the Lord God gives Himself in Revelation, who is and who was and who is to come (Revelation 1:8), here confessed of the Son.

  • v8 "hoped He was food for it" — Death takes Him for food, as it takes all; the prophet turns it the other way, He will swallow up death forever (Isaiah 25:8), and Paul quotes it, Death has been swallowed up in victory (1 Corinthians 15:54).

  • v9 "which —" — the Son's prayer breaks off in the text held here, and v10 begins the rule for when the Initiation is said. The break is kept.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

1"Let a presbyter be ordained with all the people bearing witness to him, as was said before: skilled in reading, meek, poor, not a lover of money, one who has labored much in serving the weak, proved to be pure, without blame; if he has been as a father to the orphans, if he has served the poor, if he has not grown cold in his love for the Church, if he is devout and quiet in all things, so that, being such a man, he may in every way be worthy to have what is fitting and suitable revealed to him by God, and may also be counted worthy of the gift of healing.

chapters.title: The Ordination of a Presbyter
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 30

1"Then let the appointment of the presbyter be like this. With all the priestly company leading him, the bishop laying his hand on his head and the presbyters touching him and holding him, let the bishop begin and say this:

2The Prayer of Ordination of a Presbyter

3'O God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the One beyond words, the Light, who have neither beginning nor end, the Lord, who ordered all things and set their bounds, and by reason defined the order of all that You created: hear us, and look on this servant of Yours, and make him share in, and give him, the Spirit of grace and of reason and of strength, the Spirit of the presbyterate, who does not grow old and cannot be dissolved, of one kind, loving the faithful, rebuking, so that he may help and govern Your people with labor, with fear, with a pure heart, with holiness, with excellence, with wisdom, and by the working of the Holy Spirit, through Your care, O Lord. As, when You looked on Your chosen people, You commanded Moses to ask for the elders, and filling them with Your Spirit You gave Him to Your minister, so now, O Lord, give this man in abundance Your Spirit, whom You gave to those You Yourself made disciples, and to all who through them truly believed in You. Make him worthy, filled with Your wisdom and Your hidden mysteries, to feed Your people in holiness of heart, pure and true; praising, blessing, extolling, giving thanks, always lifting up glory day and night to Your holy and glorious name; laboring with cheerfulness and patience to be a vessel of Your Holy Spirit; always having and carrying the cross of Your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom be praise and might to You with the Holy Spirit forever and ever.'

4Let both the priests and the people give him the Peace, with a holy kiss.

The presbyter, the Church's elder, is ordained on that pattern.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Presbyter's Work
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 31

1"After he is ordained, let him be constant at the altar, laboring in prayer without ceasing. Sometimes let him rest alone in some house from the things of the Lord's house, but without ceasing from prayer or cutting it short by one hour.

2Let him fast three days each week all the year, so that he may be perfected in understanding, and beyond that as his strength allows; not wandering about, going here and there with every spirit, but doing everything with energy.

3If it is revealed to a presbyter or bishop to speak, let him speak; if not, let him not neglect or despise his work.

4If it is revealed to a presbyter to visit his parishes and speak the word, let him go; if not, let him pray to God; and if it is revealed to him to speak to them, let him speak to them, always taking up the burden and load of Him who was crucified for him, and praying for all the people.

5Let a presbyter or bishop not be anxious about food or clothing. God takes thought and cares for His own in the things He knows. If, when he receives food or clothing from someone, he is told to receive from another as well, let it be enough for him to receive from the first alone, and only as far as is fitting and as he needs, not to excess.

chapters.title: The Daily Praise
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 32

1"Let them say the daily hymn of praise in the Church, each of them at his own time, like this:

2'The grace of our Lord be with you all.'

3The people say, 'And with your spirit.'

4The priest: 'Praise the Lord.'

5The people: 'It is fitting and right.'

6The priest: 'You, O Father of incorruption, Deliverer of our souls, Strengthener of our thoughts and Guardian of our hearts, who have lit up our hearts and ended the darkness of our understanding by the knowledge that is in You; who by the cross of Your Only-begotten have brought back again to incorruption the old man who was given over to corruption; who have put an end to error, and by Your commandments have brought man over to immortality; who sought what was lost: You we Your servants, and Your people too, praise.'

7The people: 'We praise You,' and the rest.

8The priest: 'We praise You, O Lord, whom the unceasing songs of glory of the archangels, the hymns of praise of the Glories and the chants of the Dominions praise without ceasing. We praise You, O Lord, who sent Your Thought, Your Word, Your Wisdom, Your Power, Him who is of old and was with You before the ages, the uncreated Word of the Uncreated, who appeared in the flesh at the end of times for the salvation of created man: Your beloved Son Jesus Christ, who made us free from the yoke of slavery. So we also, as we are accustomed, Your servants, O Lord, and Your people too, praise You.'

9The people: 'We praise You,' and the rest.

10The priest: 'We sing to You a threefold hymn of praise from our hearts, O Lord who give life: to You who visit the souls of the poor and do not neglect the spirits of the afflicted, Supporter of the persecuted, Helper of those tossed on the sea, Deliverer of those battered by the storm, Provider for the hungry, who avenge those who are wronged, Lover of the faithful, Companion of the saints, Home of the pure, Dwelling place of those who call on You in truth, Protector of widows, Liberator of orphans, who give Your Church right government, and have founded in it love feasts, ministries, the receiving of the faithful, the sharing of the Spirit, gifts of grace and powers. We praise You; we never cease to picture in our hearts the image of Your kingdom in ourselves, for Your sake and for the sake of Your beloved Son Jesus Christ, through whom be praise and might to You with the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.'

11Let the people say, 'Amen.'

12If anyone also speaks words of prophecy, let him speak them; he has a reward.

13At midnight let the sons of the priestly service, and those of the people who are more perfect, give praise by themselves; for at that hour our Lord, rising, praised His Father.

14See, children of light: whoever believes the words of the Lord walks as He walked in this world, so that where He is, he may be also.

Notes

  • v14 "walks as He walked… where He is, he may be also" — John's letter, whoever says he remains in Him ought himself to walk just as He walked (1 John 2:6), and the Lord's promise, so that where I am, you may be also (John 14:3).

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Deacon Chosen
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 33

1"The deacon is appointed, chosen as was said before: if he is of good conduct, if he is pure, if he has been chosen for purity and for freedom from distractions; if not, then if he is the husband of one wife, with all the faithful bearing witness to him, not entangled in the business of the world, not knowing a trade, without riches, without children. If he is married or has children, let his children be taught to practice devotion and to be pure, so that they may be approved by the Church according to the rule of the ministry. chapters.title: The Deacon's Work
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 34

1"Let him carry out in the Church what is right. Let his ministry be like this. First, let him do only what the bishop commands, as for a proclamation. Let him be the counselor of the whole clergy and the mystery of the Church: one who serves the sick, serves strangers, helps the widows, is the father of the orphans, and goes around all the houses of those in need, so that no one is in affliction or sickness or misery. Let him go around the houses of the catechumens, to strengthen those who doubt and teach those who are untaught.

2Let him clothe the men who have died, preparing them; let him bury strangers, and guide those who leave their homes or go into captivity. For the help of those in need let him inform the Church. Let him not trouble the bishop, but only on the first day of the week report everything, so that he may know.

3Let him be watchful at the hour of the assembly, going around the church, and see that no one there is proud, or a buffoon, or a spy, or one who speaks idle words. Let him rebuke such a one in the sight and hearing of all, and put out the one he has judged deserving of punishment, so that the others also may fear. If the offender persuades him to let him partake, let him comfort him. But if the man persists in his wrongdoing or disorder, let him report him to the bishop, and let him be kept apart seven days and then called, so that he is not taken captive. If, when he comes, he still goes on and persists in his folly, let him be cut off until, truly repenting, he comes to himself and asks to be received back.

4If he is in a city by the sea, let him go quickly around the places on the shore, in case anyone has died in the sea; let him clothe him and bury him. Let him also search the guest house in the same way, in case anyone staying there is sick or in need or dead, and let him make it known to the Church, so that it may provide what is right for each one. Let him have the paralyzed and the infirm bathed as is right, so that they may have relief from their pains. Let him give each one what is right through the Church.

5In the Church let twelve presbyters, seven deacons, fourteen subdeacons and thirteen widows who sit in front be recognized.

6Of the deacons, let the one who is thought most earnest among them, and best at governing, be chosen to receive strangers. Let him always be at the guest house that is in the church, dressed in white, with a stole only on his shoulder.

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Deacon's Call and the Prayers
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 35

The Deacon's Call

1"Let him be in everything like the eye of the Church, admonishing with fear, so that he may be an example of devotion to the people. Let him admonish like this:

2'Let everyone know his place.

3Let the catechumens depart.

4See that no one unclean, no one slothful, remains. Lift up the eyes of your hearts.

5The angels are watching.

6See that whoever does not trust withdraws.

7Let us pray in harmony.

8Let no fornicator, no angry man remain; if anyone who serves evil is here, let him withdraw.

9See: as children of light, let us ask and pray our Lord and our God and our Savior Jesus Christ.'

The Deacon's Prayers

10When the presbyter or bishop begins the prayer, let the people pray and kneel.

11Then let the deacon say this:

12'For the peace that is from heaven let us pray, that the Lord in His mercy may give us peace.

13For our faith let us pray, that the Lord may grant us to keep truly to the end the faith that is in Him.

14For harmony and concord let us pray, that the Lord may keep us together in the concord of the Spirit.

15For patience let us pray, that the Lord may give us patience to the end in all afflictions.

16For the apostles let us pray, that the Lord may grant us to please Him as they also pleased Him, and make us worthy of their inheritance.

17For the holy prophets let us pray, that the Lord may number us with them.

18For the holy confessors let us pray, that the Lord God may grant us to finish our course with the same mind as they.

19For the bishop let us pray, that our Lord may grant him to us for length of days in faith, rightly handling the word of truth, and standing at the head of the Church purely and without blame.

20For the presbyterate let us pray, that the Lord may not take the spirit of the presbyterate away from them, but give them earnestness and devotion to the end.

21For the deacons let us pray, that the Lord may grant them to run a perfect course and to perfect holiness, and that He may remember their work and their love.

22For the presbyteresses let us pray, that the Lord may hear their prayers, keep their hearts perfectly in the grace of the Spirit, and help their work.

23For the subdeacons, readers and deaconesses let us pray, that the Lord may grant them to receive a reward in patience.

24For the faithful laymen let us pray, that the Lord may grant them to keep the faith perfectly.

25For the catechumens let us pray, that the Lord may count them worthy of the washing of forgiveness, and sanctify them with the seal of holiness.

26For the kingdom let us pray, that the Lord may give it peace.

27For the exalted powers let us pray, that the Lord may give them prudence and the fear of Him.

28For all the world let us pray, that the Lord may provide for each one what is fitting.

29For those who travel by sea and those who go on journeys let us pray, that the Lord may guide them with the right hand of mercy.

30For those who are persecuted let us pray, that the Lord may give them patience and knowledge, and bring their labor to completion.

31For those of the Church who have fallen asleep let us pray, that the Lord may give them a place of rest.

32For those who have fallen let us pray, that the Lord may not hold their follies against them, but soften His threats toward them.

33Let all of us who need prayer pray also, that the Lord may protect and keep us with the peaceful Spirit.

34Let us entreat and pray the Lord, that He may receive our prayers.'

35When the deacon has made the remembrance, let the bishop make a sign with his hand.

36Let the deacon say, 'Let us rise in the Holy Spirit, so that, made wise, we may grow in His grace, boasting in His name. Built on the foundation of the apostles, let us ask and pray the Lord that He may be moved to receive our prayers.'

37Then let the bishop complete the prayer, and let the people say, 'Amen.'

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Lambs or Wolves
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 36

1"Let the deacon be such a man that he appears with fear, modesty and reverence. In fervor of spirit let him have a complete way of life. Let him watch and look at those who enter the house of the sanctuary, and find out who they are, so that he may know whether they are lambs or wolves. When he asks, let him bring in the one who is worthy; otherwise, if a spy enters, the freedom of the Church will be searched out, and his sin will be on his head.

2If anyone comes late to the praise, either when the praise of the dawn is being said or when the Offering is being offered, whoever he is, let him stay outside, and let the deacon not bring him in. It is a type of the day of judgment to come, and the noise of his entering would distract those who are praying. When he comes and finds the door shut, let him not knock, because of what has been said.

3After the hymn of praise that comes first is finished, let the faithful man or faithful woman enter. Let the deacon say, either over the Offering or for the hymn of praise, 'Let us pray that the Lord may write our prayer in the book of life, and that God, who is forever, may remember us in His holy dwellings of light. For this brother who is late, let us pray that the Lord may give him earnestness and labor, turn away from him every bond of this world, and give him the will of affection and love and hope.'

4Likewise for a sister or a deaconess, for those who are late or stay outside, let him urge all the people to pray for them. For when a deacon names them and urges this, earnestness is strengthened, the bond of love is fulfilled, and the scorner and the slothful are disciplined.

chapters.title: A Woman Wronged
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 37

1"If any woman suffers violence from a man, let the deacon find out carefully whether she is one of the faithful and has truly suffered violence, and whether the man who did it was not her lover. If it is truly so, and she mourns over the violence done to her, let him bring it to the bishop's hearing, so that she may be shown to be in communion with the Church in all things. If the man who did her violence is one of the faithful, let the deacon not bring him into the church to partake, even if he repents. But if he is a catechumen and repents, let him be baptized and partake. Let the deacon instruct those who repent and bring them to the presbyters or to the bishop, so that they may be instructed and taught knowledge. But if his power suffices to carry out the office of the diaconate perfectly, let him stay only in prayer. Let him count as his work prayer and meditation, love, the way, mourning, and keeping fear before his eyes; and he will be called a son of light.

1"Let the appointment of a deacon be like this. Let the bishop alone lay a hand on him, because he is appointed not to the priesthood but to the service of attending on the bishop and the Church. Over the deacon, then, let the bishop say this:

2The Prayer of Ordination of a Deacon

chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 39

1"If anyone is attested and confesses that he was in chains and in prison and in afflictions for the name of God, a hand is not laid on him for the diaconate on that account, nor for the presbyterate. He has the honor of the clergy, having been protected by the hand of God through his confession. But if he is appointed bishop, he is also counted worthy of the laying on of the hand. Even if he is a confessor who has not been judged before the authorities and has not been beaten in chains, but has only confessed, he is counted worthy of the laying on of the hand, for he receives the prayer of the clergy. But let the bishop not pray over him repeating all these words; when the shepherd goes forward, he will receive the effect.
