chapters.title: The Widow Chosen
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 40

1"Let a widow be appointed when she is chosen, if she has long remained without a husband, and if, though often pressed by men to marry, she has not married, because of the faith. If not, it is not yet right that she be chosen; let her be tested for a time: whether she is devout; whether, if she has children, she has brought them up in holiness, has not taught them worldly wisdom, and has made them examples of the holy law and of the Church; whether she has loved and honored strangers, has been constant in prayer, has lived meekly, and has gladly helped the afflicted; whether it has been revealed to the saints about her; whether she has not neglected the saints, and has served with all her strength; whether she is fit to bear and endure the burden, praying without ceasing, complete in all things, fervent in spirit, with the eyes of her heart opened in everything, always kind, loving innocence, owning nothing in this world, but always taking up and carrying the cross, crucifying all evil, staying by the altar night and day, working gladly and in secret. If she has one or two or three of like mind in My name, I am among them. Let her be complete in the Lord, as one who is visited by the Spirit. Let her do what is made known to her with fear and earnestness. Let her instruct the women who do not obey, teach those who have not learned, turn back those who are foolish, and instruct them to be serious. Let her test the deaconesses; let her make those who come in know what sort of people they are and who they are, and instruct them to stay. To those who listen let her patiently give the counsel that is proper; to those who are disobedient after three instructions let her not speak. Let her love those who wish to live in virginity or in purity, and correct those who oppose themselves modestly and quietly. Let her be at peace with everyone. Let her privately shut the mouths of those who talk much and idly; if they do not listen, let her take an older woman with her, or bring it to the bishop's hearing. In the church let her be silent. In prayer let her be persistent. Let her visit the women who are sick, and each first day of the week take one or two deacons with her and help them. If she has any possessions, let her give them to the poor and the faithful; if she has nothing, let the Church help her. Let her do no worldly work, as though for a trial, but have these works of the Spirit: let her continue in prayer and fasting, ask for nothing great, receive what the Lord gives, and not be anxious for her children, but hand them over to the Church, so that living in the house of God they may be fit for the service of the priesthood. Her requests to God will be acceptable; they are the sacrifice and altar of God. For those who have served well will be praised by the archangels. But as for those who are dissolute and raging and drunken, babblers and busybodies and evil, those who love pleasures much, the figures of their souls, which stand before the Father of lights, perish and are carried away to live in darkness; or their visible deeds, going up before the Most High, drag them easily to the pit, so that, after this world is changed and passes away, the figures of their souls may stand against them as witnesses and not let them look up. For the figure and type of every soul stands before God from the foundation of the world. So let her be chosen who can go to meet the holy bowls. To them belong the twelve presbyters who praise My Father who is in heaven, who receive the prayers of every holy soul and offer them to the Most High as a soothing aroma.

Notes

  • v1 "the holy bowls… who receive the prayers of every holy soul" — John's vision of heaven: the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints (Revelation 5:8). Here the elders are twelve, and the widow chosen is one fit to go and meet them.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Widow's Appointment
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 41

1"Let the appointment be like this. As she prays at the entrance of the altar, looking down, let the bishop say quietly, so that the priests may hear:

2The Prayer of the Appointment of Widows Who Sit in Front

3'O God, the Holy One, the Most High, who see what is lowly, who have chosen the weak and the mighty; the Honored One, who created also what is despised: give, O Lord, the spirit of power to this handmaid of Yours, and strengthen her with Your truth, so that, doing Your commandment and serving in the house of Your sanctuary, she may be an honored vessel for You, and may glorify You on the day when You glorify Your poor, O Lord. Grant her power to carry out gladly Your teachings, which You have set as a rule for Your handmaid. Grant her, O Lord, the spirit of meekness and of power and of patience and of kindness, so that, bearing Your burden with joy beyond words, she may endure labors. Yes, O Lord God, who know our weakness, perfect Your handmaid for the praise of Your house; strengthen her for building up and for a good example; sanctify her, make her wise, comfort her, O God. For blessed and glorious is Your kingdom, O God the Father, and to You be praise, and to Your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the Holy Spirit, good and worthy of worship, Maker of life, of one being with You, now and before all the ages and for the ages and forever and ever.' The people: 'Amen.'

Notes

  • v3 "who have chosen the weak… who created also what is despised" — Paul's words: God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong; God chose what is low and despised in the world (1 Corinthians 1:27–28).

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Widow's Rule
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 42

1"After she is appointed like this, let her not be anxious about anything, but live alone and be free for devout prayer. For the foundation of holiness and life for such a widow is solitude, for she has loved no one but the God of gods, the Father who is in heaven. At the fixed times let her give praise by herself, at night and at dawn. If she is in her monthly period, let her stay in the temple and not come near the altar, not as though she were unclean, but so that the altar may have honor. Afterward, when she has fasted and bathed, let her be constant at the altar. In the days of Pentecost let her not fast. At the feast of Pascha let her give what she has to the poor, bathe, and then pray. When she gives thanks or praise, if she has friends, virgins of like mind, it is good that they pray with her for the sake of the Amen; if not, let her pray alone, in the church and in the house, above all at midnight. The times when she should give praise are the Sabbath, the first day of the week, Pascha, Epiphany and Pentecost. At other times let her give thanks meekly with psalms, hymns of praise and meditations, and labor like this. For the Most High will sanctify them and forgive all their sins, those that were written against them before, and their error. My Father, the Heavenly One, will strengthen them and make their faces shine like the faces of

2My sanctuaries; they will shine in My glory on the day of reward.

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Widow's Hymn
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 43

1"Let her hymns of praise be said quietly, like this:

2'Holy, holy, without spot, who have Your dwelling in the light, God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, God of Enoch and David, of Elijah, of Elisha, of Moses, of Joshua, and of the prophets and the others who preached Your name in truth, God of the apostles, the God who have guided all things by Your reason and blessed those who trust in You with love: my soul praises You with the power of the spirit of my strength; my heart praises You, O Lord, and Your might, always. Let all my strength praise You, O Lord, for if You will, I am Yours, O God, the God of the poor; for You are the Helper of those in need, the One who looks on the meek, and the Supporter of the weak. Help me, O Lord, for by Your grace You were pleased in me that I should be Your handmaid, for You have given me a great name, that I should be called a Christian. You freed me from slavery so that I may serve as a slave to God, the Mighty One who is forever, who sees all, so that I may praise You without condemnation. Yes, O Lord God, strengthen my heart in You until it is made complete in the Holy Spirit. Make us young again for the building up of Your holy Church, Son and Word and Thought of the Father, the Christ who came for the salvation of the human race, who suffered and was buried and rose, and was glorified by Him who sent You. Turn, help, O Lord, set our thoughts upright by the strong faith of the Spirit. Glorify Your name in us.'

chapters.title: Virgins, Men and Women
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 46

1Of Male and Female Virgins

2"A male or female virgin is not appointed or ordained by man, but is set apart of his own will and is called a virgin.

4A hand is not laid on him for virginity, for this setting apart is of their own free will. But it is right for virgins to be fixed and bound in the suffering of a sound body, to be constant in fasting and in prayer, in weeping and in mourning daily, always to expect their departure from the flesh, and to strive as people about to depart. Let them not serve rage or debauchery or drunkenness or empty talk, or be taken up with worldly work or distraction; they are as one who is on the cross. Let their hearts be lifted up, with all meekness and seemliness of thought, with meditation on the Holy Scriptures, with faithful thoughts and kind comforts, so that when they pray they may be answered in what they ask for the faithful who wish to provide for them. Let them not despise these things, so that through them also a share of life may be given to those who provide for them. Let them be strengthened in love and kindness and in true and perfect grace. Let them be constant in comforting, comforting their neighbors, instructing and teaching those who have lately become faithful, in understanding and in knowledge and in kindness, stirring up the very young, examples of holiness among them in all good things. Let the women do the same. Let them speak and work in order and in grace and in knowledge, so that they may truly be the salt of the earth, as it is said. Let the women who are virgins cover their heads in the church, hiding only their hair; and let them be counted worthy of honor by everyone, so that the rest of the women who wish to may follow their example.

5If anyone among the people appears to have a gift of healing or of knowledge or of tongues, a hand is not laid on him, for the work is plain to see. But let them have honor.

6The First Book of Clement is ended.

Notes

  • v3 — the paragraph numbered 3 in the text held here is the edition's footnote to v2, not part of the text, so no verse stands there.

  • v6 "The First Book of Clement is ended" — the close of Cooper and Maclean's first book, as the Syriac gives it; their second book follows as chapters 47–73.

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

Of Male and Female Virgins
"A male or female virgin is not appointed or ordained by man, but is set apart of his own will and is called a virgin.

A hand is not laid on him for virginity, for this setting apart is of their own free will. But it is right for virgins to be fixed and bound in the suffering of a sound body, to be constant in fasting and in prayer, in weeping and in mourning daily, always to expect their departure from the flesh, and to strive as people about to depart. Let them not serve rage or debauchery or drunkenness or empty talk, or be taken up with worldly work or distraction; they are as one who is on the cross. Let their hearts be lifted up, with all meekness and seemliness of thought, with meditation on the Holy Scriptures, with faithful thoughts and kind comforts, so that when they pray they may be answered in what they ask for the faithful who wish to provide for them. Let them not despise these things, so that through them also a share of life may be given to those who provide for them. Let them be strengthened in love and kindness and in true and perfect grace. Let them be constant in comforting, comforting their neighbors, instructing and teaching those who have lately become faithful, in understanding and in knowledge and in kindness, stirring up the very young, examples of holiness among them in all good things. Let the women do the same. Let them speak and work in order and in grace and in knowledge, so that they may truly be the salt of the earth, as it is said. Let the women who are virgins cover their heads in the church, hiding only their hair; and let them be counted worthy of honor by everyone, so that the rest of the women who wish to may follow their example.
If anyone among the people appears to have a gift of healing or of knowledge or of tongues, a hand is not laid on him, for the work is plain to see. But let them have honor.
The First Book of Clement is ended.

chapters.title: Those Who Come to Hear
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 47

1"Let those who come for the first time to hear the Word first go to teachers at home, before they come in among all the people, and let the whole reason for their coming be examined with all care, so that their teachers may know why they have come and with what will. If they have come with good will and love, let them be taught diligently. Let those who bring them be well on in years, faithful people known to the Church, and let them bear witness about them, whether they are able to hear the word. Let their life and conduct also be asked about: whether they are not quarrelsome; whether they are quiet and meek, not speakers of empty things or scorners or foul-mouthed, or buffoons or misleaders or mockers. Let it be asked too whether any of them has a wife or not. If, of his own free will, he has no wife, let him be instructed carefully and diligently and persuaded with all kindness to amend his failings. Let the bishop provide for him in the Lord with the instructions of the prophets that lead him to purity; and if he makes progress, with the teachings of the apostles, then of the Gospels, and with the perfect word of teaching; and if he is worthy, let him be baptized. If he is then worthy of the hidden things, let him hear them by himself, and make progress also in what is hidden.

2Let there be no obstacle at all to the one who wishes to marry, so that he is not caught by the Evil One through fornication. But let him marry a Christian, a faithful woman of the Christian people, who is able to keep her husband in the faith, at the bishop's bidding, as he provides for him.

3Let the one who comes also be asked whether he is a slave or free. If he is the slave of one who is faithful, and his master permits him, let him hear. If his master is not faithful and does not permit him, let him be persuaded to permit him. If his master says truly of him that he wishes to become a Christian because he hates his masters, let him be cast out. But if no reason of hatred of slavery is shown, and he truly wishes to be a Christian, let him hear. If his master is faithful and does not bear witness to him, let him be cast out. Likewise, if a woman is a man's wife, let her be taught to please her husband in the fear of God. If both of them wish to serve purity in devotion, they have a reward.

Notes

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Who May Not Be Received
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 48

1"If a prostitute, or a brothel keeper, or a drunkard, or a maker of idols, or a painter, or one who works in the shows, or a charioteer, or a wrestler, or one who goes to the contests, or a fighter in the games, or one who teaches wrestling, or a public huntsman, or a priest of idols or a keeper of them is among those who come, let him not be received.

2If any such person wishes to become faithful, let him give these things up; and once he is faithful in deed and baptized, let him be received and let him partake. If he does not give them up, let him be rejected.

3If anyone is a teacher of boys in worldly wisdom, it is good if he gives it up. But if he has no other trade to live by, let him be excused.

4If anyone is a soldier or in authority, let him be taught not to oppress or to kill or to rob, or to be angry or to rage at anyone and afflict him, but to be content with the rations given him. But if they wish to be baptized in the Lord, let them give up military service or the post of authority; if not, let them not be received.

5If a catechumen or a believer of the people wishes to be a soldier, let him either give up his intention or be rejected. For he has despised God in his thought; leaving the things of the Spirit, he has made himself complete in the flesh and treated the faith with contempt.

6If a prostitute or a dissolute man or a drunkard stops doing these things and, believing, wishes to become a catechumen, they may be admitted. If they make progress, let them be baptized; if not, let them be rejected.

7If a man's concubine is a slave and wishes to be faithful, if she brings up the children born to her and separates from her master, or is joined to him alone in marriage, let her hear; and once baptized let her share in the Offering. If not, let her be rejected.

8One who does things that may not be spoken of, or a diviner, or a magician, or a necromancer: these are defiled and do not come to judgment. Let a charmer, or an astrologer, or an interpreter of dreams, or a sorcerer, or one who gathers the people together, or a stargazer, or a diviner by idols either stop, and when he stops let him be exorcised and baptized; or if not, let him be rejected.

9If a man has a concubine, let him put her away, marry according to the law, and hear the word of instruction.

Notes

  • v4 "content with the rations given him" — John the Baptist to the soldiers: Do not extort money from anyone by force or by false accusation, and be content with your wages (Luke 3:14). Here John's rule is the rule for a soldier who is learning; one who wishes to be baptized must leave the army.

1st Book of the Covenant 49

1"Let the one who is being instructed with all care and hears the fullness of the Gospel be instructed for no less than three years; and if, out of love, he strives to be baptized, let him then be baptized.

chapters.title: Where Each One Stands
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 50

1"When the teacher stops, let those who are being instructed pray apart from the faithful and go out, so that the faithful may learn when the presbyter or deacon reads the New Testament or the Gospels.

2Let the faithful women stand in the church by themselves, and the women catechumens by themselves, apart from the faithful women; but all the women apart from the men, and the girls apart too, each in her order.

3The men on the right and the women on the left; the faithful virgins first, and behind them the women who are being instructed for virginity.

4After the prayer let the women catechumens give the Peace to one another, men to men and women to women.

5Let every woman cover her head, her hair too. Let the women show their modesty becomingly and seemly in their adornment, and let them not be adorned with braided hair or precious stones, or the young men who are in the church will be caught, but with modesty and knowledge. If not, let them be instructed by the widows who sit in front; and if they rebel and resist, let the bishop rebuke them.

Notes

  • v5 "not… with braided hair or precious stones" — Paul's rule for the women: with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly clothes (1 Timothy 2:9).

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Prayer over the Catechumens
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 51

1"After the catechumens pray, let the bishop or presbyter lay a hand on them and say the prayer of the laying on of the hand of the catechumens:

2'O God, who send thunders and prepare lightnings, who founded the heaven and established the earth, who give light to the faithful and turn back those who go astray; who gave life to those who were dead and hope to those who were without hope, and freed the universe from error by the coming down of Your Only-begotten Son Jesus Christ: hear us, O Lord, and give these souls understanding, completeness, undoubting faith and knowledge of the truth, so that they may come to a rank higher than this, through the holy name of You and of Your beloved Son Jesus, our Lord, through whom be praise and might to You with the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.'

3After this let them be dismissed. If anyone who is a catechumen is arrested for My name and tried with tortures, and hurries and presses on to receive the washing, let the shepherd not hesitate, but give it to him. If he suffers violence and is killed without having received the washing, let him not be anxious; for he has been baptized in his own blood, and is justified.

Notes

  • v3 "baptized in his own blood" — the catechumen killed for the Name before he reaches the water lacks nothing: his death is his baptism. The Lord spoke of His own death in the same word: I have a baptism to be baptized with (Luke 12:50).

chapters.title: The Exorcism
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 53

1"On the Sabbath let the bishop gather those who are to receive the washing, and have them kneel while the deacon makes the proclamation. When there is silence, let him exorcise them, laying a hand on them and saying:

2'O God of heaven, God of the lights, God of the archangels who are under Your power, God of the angels who are under Your might, King of glories and of dominions, God of the saints, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ; who loosed the souls bound by death; who gave light to the one bound in darkness and made him firm through the firmness of the suffering of Your Only-begotten; who loosed our cords and lifted every weight from us; who drove back from us every attack of the Evil One; O Son and Word of God, who made us immortal by Your death, who glorified us with Your glory, who loosed all the bonds of our sins by Your passion, who bore the curse of our sins by Your cross, and by Your resurrection taught mankind to pass from being sons of men to becoming gods; who took our humiliation on Yourself, who trod the way to heaven for us, who changed us from corruption to incorruption: hear me, O Lord, who cry to You in pain and fear, O Lord God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, before Him before whom stand the holy hosts of archangels and of cherubim and armies without number, of princes and of seraphim; whose veil is the light, and before whose face is fire; the throne of whose glory is beyond words; the dwellings of whose delights, which You have prepared for Your saints, are beyond words, whose robes and treasures are seen by You alone and by Your holy angels; before whom all things tremble, giving praise; whose glance measures the mountains, and whose name, when it is spoken, splits the depths; whom the heavens, shut up by Your hand, hide from view; before whom the earth and the depths together tremble; before whom the sea and the dragons in it quake; before whom the wild beasts stand trembling in awe; through whom the mountains and the foundations of the earth melt with fear; at whose power the winter storm quakes and trembles, and the raging whirlwind keeps its limits; because of whom the fire of vengeance does not pass the bound set for it, but stays when rebuked by Your commandment; because of whom the whole creation is in labor, groaning, bidden to wait until its time; from whom all nature and creation that sets itself against You flees; because of whom the whole army of the adversary is subdued, the Devil fallen, the serpent trodden down and the dragon killed; because of whom the nations that have confessed You are given light and strengthened in You, O Lord; because of whom life is revealed, hope made firm, faith strengthened and the Gospel preached; because of whom corruption is brought to nothing and incorruption grows strong; through whom man was formed from the earth, but, having believed in You, is no longer earth: O Lord God Almighty, I exorcise these in the name of You and of Your beloved Son Jesus Christ.

3Drive away from the souls of these servants of Yours every disease and illness, every stumbling block and all unbelief, all doubt and all contempt, every unclean spirit that is at work: that is a witch, that kills, that is under the earth, that is fiery, dark, foul-smelling, given to witchcraft, lustful, gold-loving, proud, money-loving, wrathful.

4Yes, O Lord God, overthrow from these servants of Yours, who have been named in You, the weapons of the Devil: all magic, witchcraft, fear of idols, divination, astrology, necromancy, watching the stars, stargazing, pleasure in the passions, love of what is shameful, sadness, love of money, drunkenness, fornication, adultery, lust, defiance, quarreling, wrath, confusion, wickedness, evil suspicion. Yes, O Lord God, hear me, and breathe on these servants of Yours the spirit of calm, so that, guarded by You, they may bear in You the fruits of faith, of virtue, of wisdom, of purity, of self-discipline, of patience, of hope, of concord, of modesty, of praise. For by You they have been called as servants, in the name of Jesus Christ, being baptized in the Trinity, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, with the angels, glories, dominions and all the army of heaven as witnesses. O Lord, the true being of our life and theirs, guard their hearts, O God, for You are mighty and glorious forever and ever.'

5Let all the people, and the priests too, say, 'Amen. So be it, so be it, so be it.'

6If anyone who is enduring anything rises suddenly while the bishop is saying these words, and weeps or cries out, or foams at the mouth or grinds his teeth, or stares, or is greatly lifted up, or runs away altogether, quickly carried off, let him be put aside by the deacons, so that there is no disturbance while the bishop is speaking. Let him be exorcised by the priests until he is cleansed, and then let him be baptized.

7After the priest has exorcised those who have drawn near, or the one found unclean, let him breathe on them and seal them between the eyes, on the nose, on the heart and on the ears; and then let him raise them up.

Notes

  • v2 "the whole creation is in labor, groaning, bidden to wait until its time" — Paul's words: the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until now (Romans 8:22). In the same prayer the Son teaches mankind to pass from being sons of men to becoming gods, as the morning praise says of those who trust in Him (26:19).

  • Source text — J. Cooper and A. J. Maclean, The Testament of Our Lord, translated into English from the Syriac (1902), public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 54

1"In the forty days of Pascha, let the people stay in the —

2When he takes hold of each one, let him ask, the one being baptized turning to the west, and let him say, 'Say: I renounce you, Satan, and all your service, your shows, your pleasures and all your works.' When he has said these things and confessed, let him be anointed with the oil that was exorcised, the one who anoints him saying, 'I anoint you with this oil of exorcism, for deliverance from every evil and unclean spirit and from every evil.' Then, turning him to the east, let him say, 'Say: I submit to You, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, before whom all nature trembles and is moved. Grant me to do all Your will without blame.'

3After these things let him hand him over to the presbyter who baptizes, and let them stand in the water naked, and let the deacon go down with him likewise. When the one being baptized goes down into the water, let the one who baptizes him put his hand on him and say, 'Do you believe in God the Father Almighty?' Let the one being baptized say, 'I believe.' Let him at once baptize him once. Let the priest also say, 'Do you believe also in Christ Jesus the Son of God, who came from the Father, who is of old with the Father, who was born of Mary the Virgin by the Holy Spirit, who was crucified in the days of Pontius Pilate, and died, and rose the third day, came to life from the dead, ascended into heaven, sat down at the right hand of the Father, and is coming to judge the living and the dead?' When he says, 'I believe,' let him baptize him the second time. Let him also say, 'Do you believe also in the Holy Spirit, in the holy Church?' Let the one being baptized say, 'I believe,' and then let him baptize him the third time.

chapters.title: The Laying On of Hands and the Seal
chapters.html:
1st Book of the Covenant 55

1"Then let them be together in the church, and let the bishop lay a hand on them after baptism, saying and calling down over them:

2'O Lord God, who through Your beloved Son Jesus Christ filled Your holy apostles with the Holy Spirit, and by the Spirit let Your blessed prophets speak; who counted these servants of Yours worthy of forgiveness of sins in Your Christ through the washing of rebirth, and cleansed them of all the mist of error and the darkness of unbelief: make them worthy to be filled with Your Holy Spirit, by Your love for mankind, giving them Your grace, so that they may serve You according to Your will, truly, O God, do Your commandments in holiness, and, always tending what is of Your will, enter into Your eternal dwellings, through You and through Your beloved Son Jesus Christ, through whom be praise and might to You with the Holy Spirit forever and ever.'

3Likewise, pouring the oil and placing a hand on his head, let him say, 'I anoint you in God Almighty, and in Jesus Christ, and in the Holy Spirit, so that you may be His soldier, with a perfect faith, a vessel pleasing to Him.'

4Sealing him on his forehead, let him give him the Peace and say, 'The Lord God of the meek be with you.' Let the one who has been sealed answer, 'And with your spirit.' So for each one in turn.

1"From then on let them pray together with all the people. Let the offering be brought by the deacon, and then let the shepherd give thanks. The bread is offered as a type of My body.
